P1.evidence: No setter on this call — inbound from Trevor's YouTube — so the read-back check does not apply. The frame was the usual two-part version: "calls pretty basic though I just want to get a good idea where you're at, you know build out what it is that you want if there's alignment let's talk about it if not it's fine alrighty", with no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need' and agreement assumed rather than asked. The open question ran and was well anchored to what the prospect had already said: "you said you're looking for a trainer what is it that you were hoping we could potentially help you with man?" Worth noting for a coach: the frame arrived at 00:05:11, after roughly five minutes in which the rep asked the prospect for travel recommendations for his own US trip.

P2.evidence: One check out of nine. "Are you training now, or not really?" was asked and produced a good picture — sauna, cold plunge, ATG, basketball, no regimented training. Everything else was either volunteered or absent. Age came out in the prospect's own monologue ("I'm also 38, 39 next week"); height and weight were never asked. Work was never asked — "I'm in the pot business" was volunteered, and the only ownership question came at 00:26:35, after the price, in order to offer a tax write-off. No health-conditions question and no injury question at all: the prospect volunteered back surgery, a car wreck and a period of not being able to walk at 00:06:00 and the rep's entire response was to move on. Diet was never asked ("I eat pretty damn healthy" was volunteered). No sleep, no energy. This is the phase that exists to catch exactly what this prospect disclosed, and it was not run.

P3.evidence: Stopped at the surface. The six-month question was asked — "if we were to be six months down the line, what's really the, what would you be happy with? What's success?" — and produced muscle mass, flexibility and nutritional understanding, which the rep reflected back accurately: "Sounds like a lot of it's about more of the understanding as well, rather than just like, give me a load of instructions." That is where it ended. No 'something physical you want to do but can't' — despite the prospect having just described riding and skiing less aggressively out of fear. No bridge to what is actually driving it, no 'what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact', nothing about family, identity or longevity. On a prospect turning 39 who has already had a spinal surgery, the material for the deep half of this phase was sitting in the open.

P4.evidence: Reached the right answer by an unscripted route. Instead of the past-attempts sequence, the rep asked what changed and then how the prospect likes to be coached, using a story about another client as the prompt. That produced the gap in the prospect's own words: "I would say partially, you know, it's the accountability, right? Inconsistency. I tend to like jump around on different like ATG exercises or YouTube exercises, morning routines." Nothing was asked about what he had tried before, what happened with it, or why it did not stick, and the 'information isn't the problem' line was never run even though the prospect twice said his issue was not knowing enough.

P5.evidence: Not attempted. The rep went from the coaching-style question straight to "All right, dude. Well, I'll walk you through it. I'll go through, like, the philosophy of it first." No two-year question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The obvious consequence frame — a 39-year-old with a fused-or-repaired back who is already losing confidence on a mountain bike, projected forward two years — was never built.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The belief question was never asked, the all-in question was never asked, and the offer and price were presented without a verbal yes in hand. The prospect asked the cost twice ("What is it? Does cost like monthly or?" and later "what is the total cost again for six months?") before the rep had established anything to price it against.

P11.evidence: The recording ends at 00:28:36 during the scheduling conversation, immediately after the guarantee and before any close was attempted. None of the four steps had happened by that point, but the phase was cut off rather than skipped, so it is scored not_applicable rather than missed.

objection_plays.detail: Raised honestly by the prospect as his single stated worry: "the only worry for me and I'm just trying to be straight up for you is like when I travel for work... Those sometimes, like, deals, I just can't miss it." The rep neutralised it without running the play — social proof plus the pause policy: "probably 65-70% of our clients are business owners who travel a lot. We tailor everything to that" and "worst case scenario is if you go into, like, Myanmar or something, then we can pause it." Effective and the prospect closed it out with "Sweet." None of the scripted moves ran, but the objection did not need them; scored partial because the outcome was achieved by improvisation rather than by the play.

Script gap, and the important one on this call. The prospect disclosed post-surgical spinal history and current symptoms — "I had back surgery a couple years ago, got in a car wreck, and, like, couldn't walk for a while" and "my back, like, after basketball... I'm still feeling it" — which is a clinical-fit question, not an objection the prospect ever raised. The playbook has no move for it: no screening question, no clearance step, no rule about when a prospect must be referred back to a clinician before loaded ballistic work is recommended. The known_gaps list already records that there is no play for a clinical or medical-fit objection when the prospect raises it; this call shows the sharper version of the gap, where nobody raises it at all and the process has nothing that forces the question.

Second gap. The prospect's incumbent is the ATG / Knees Over Toes method, which he says outperformed his post-surgical physical therapy — "It helped after the surgery more than physical therapy" — and he asked directly whether he could keep doing it. The rep said yes and moved on. There is no scripted handling for a cheap or free method that demonstrably worked for the prospect, which is the same gap the playbook already logs from the Badrane Hriouch call. Accommodating it is not the same as differentiating from it.

notes: One baseline question out of nine, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and a spinal surgery disclosure that drew zero follow-up before loaded ballistic training was recommended. The rep is likeable and the travel objection was handled well, but the front five minutes went on his own holiday plans and the discovery never recovered. The coaching point that matters is not sequence here — it is that a prospect saying 'I couldn't walk for a while' has to stop the call and start a medical conversation.
